title: Minimum Cost to Cut a Stick
description: Given a wooden stick of length `n` and an array of integers `cuts` where `cuts[i]` denotes a position where you should perform a cut. The cost of one cut is the length of the stick being cut. Return the minimum total cost of the cuts.
input_format: First line contains `n` and `m` (number of cuts). Second line contains `m` cuts.
hints: Add boundary points 0 and n to the cuts array and sort them.
Let `dp[i][j]` be the minimum cost to make all cuts between cuts[i] and cuts[j].
Try every cut `cuts[k]` as the first cut in this interval.

reference_solution:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n, m = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    cuts = sorted([int(x) for x in data[2:2+m]])
    cuts = [0] + cuts + [n]
    k = len(cuts)
    dp = [[0]*k for _ in range(k)]
    for length in range(2, k):
        for i in range(k - length):
            j = i + length
            dp[i][j] = min(dp[i][m_idx] + dp[m_idx][j] for m_idx in range(i+1, j)) + (cuts[j] - cuts[i])
    print(dp[0][k-1])
